verses.text: Samson went down to Timnah, and there he saw a young Philistine woman.
When he came back, he told his father and mother, "I have seen a Philistine woman in Timnah. Now get her for me as my wife."

His father and mother answered, "Is there not a suitable woman among your relatives or among all our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?" But Samson told his father, "Get her for me. She is the right one for me."
His parents did not know that this was from the LORD, who was looking for a chance to act against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. As they came to the vineyards of Timnah, suddenly a young lion came roaring toward him.
The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully on Samson, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as easily as he might tear a young goat. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
Then he went down and talked with the woman, and he liked her very much.
Some time later, when he went back to marry her, he turned aside to look at the lion's body. In it was a swarm of bees and some honey.

He scooped out the honey with his hands and ate it as he walked along. When he came back to his parents, he gave them some, and they ate it too. But he did not tell them he had taken the honey from the lion's body.
Then his father went down to see the woman. And Samson held a feast there, as was the custom for young men.
When the people saw him, they chose thirty young men to be his companions.
Samson said to them, "Let me tell you a riddle. If you can give me the answer within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen shirts and thirty sets of clothes.
If you cannot tell me the answer, you must give me thirty linen shirts and thirty sets of clothes." "Tell us your riddle," they said. "Let us hear it."
He replied, "Out of the eater came something to eat. Out of the strong came something sweet." For three days they could not give the answer.
On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Trick your husband into telling us the answer to the riddle, or we will burn you and your father's family to death. Did you invite us here to rob us?"

Then Samson's wife cried in front of him and said, "You hate me! You do not really love me. You have given my people a riddle, but you have not told me the answer." "I have not even told my father or mother," he replied, "so why should I tell you?"
She cried the rest of the seven days of the feast. On the seventh day he finally told her, because she kept pushing him. She in turn told the answer to her people.

Before sunset on the seventh day the men of the town said to him, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" Samson said to them, "If you had not ploughed with my young cow, you would not have solved my riddle."

Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully on him. He went down to Ashkelon, struck down thirty of their men, took their belongings and gave their clothes to those who had answered the riddle. Burning with anger, he went back up to his father's home.
And Samson's wife was given to one of his companions who had been his best man.
